headline: Highest risk is data leakage: aci’s broad network egress and CRM/email data can flow into authelia’s OIDC/ForwardAuth path, while prompt-injection and capability-conflict risks are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use direct function calls or MCP and touches email/CRM/research data; authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth and broad network egress. If aci output is bridged into authelia-managed auth flows or shared files, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF aci outputs are copied into a shared MCP/file channel consumed by authelia-managed workflows, injection becomes plausible.
IF authelia parses upstream text from aci as policy or routing instructions, prompt injection is reachable.
mitigations: Disable any shared MCP or file bridge between the agents.
Require structured JSON schemas for all aci-to-authelia handoffs.
Add a manual review step before authelia consumes aci-generated text.
Log and reject nonconforming control tokens in handoff payloads.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci explicitly touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; authelia also has broad network egress and handles OIDC/ForwardAuth. In a shared workspace or auth flow, sensitive data can leave the pair to third-party services. Because both agents are docs-only and the exact deployment is unclear, I keep this at high rather than critical.
conditions: IF aci and authelia share a workspace, CRM/email data can be exposed across the pair.
IF either agent forwards context into external APIs during OIDC/ForwardAuth handling, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Isolate each agent in separate workspaces.
Remove sensitive fields from aci outputs before handoff.
Restrict authelia to minimal auth metadata only.
Turn off any debug or verbose logging that captures payloads.
Use a redaction proxy for email, CRM, and calendar content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API calls, while authelia is not runnable and has no subprocess or browser capability. There is some overlap on networked integrations, but no evidence of shared writable filesystem, git, or database state. The pair therefore has limited write-conflict surface and the main risk is coordination, not direct contention.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external API resource, concurrent updates can race.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents to the same OAuth principal, overlapping writes become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts.
Serialize writes to shared external systems.
Add optimistic-lock checks on mutable records.
Keep authelia read-only where possible.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and authelia can enforce OIDC/ForwardAuth decisions. If authelia consumes aci outputs without verification, a mistaken or manipulated recommendation can cascade into access-control or routing errors. The pathway is inferred from documented surfaces rather than directly observed, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF authelia treats aci-generated text as authoritative policy input, errors cascade.
IF aci produces incorrect identity or routing metadata that authelia applies without validation, downstream actions can be wrong.
mitigations: Require explicit validation before authelia acts on aci output.
Add a human approval gate for access-control changes.
Compare aci outputs against source-of-truth identity data.
Record provenance for every handoff field.

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, support, and calendar data, which often carry regulated personal data, while authelia performs authentication and ForwardAuth/OIDC functions with broad network egress. If the pair processes EU PII or similar sensitive data through external auth or logging paths, retention and residency mismatches are plausible. The profiles do not specify jurisdictions, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF EU personal data is routed through authelia-backed auth logs, residency/compliance issues arise.
IF aci stores CRM or email content in external services without matching retention controls, policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Minimize logged fields in both agents.
Set explicit retention limits for auth and CRM records.
Route regulated data only through approved regions.
Document a DPA and data-flow map before deployment.
